editorial.approach: You can reverse a string by converting it to an array of characters, swapping elements using two pointers, and joining it back into a string.

hints: JavaScript strings are immutable, so you'll need to build a new string or convert it to an array first.
Using built-in methods, you can split, reverse, and join.
To do it manually, iterate through the string backwards and concatenate characters to a new string.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Iterate backwards from the last index of the string to 0, concatenating each character to a new string.
bruteForceSolution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) (due to string concatenation copy operations in JavaScript)

optimizedSolution.explanation: Convert the string to an array, reverse the array in-place using two pointers (swapping elements from outer ends inward), and then join it back to a string.

interviewExplanation: In JavaScript, string concatenation `s += char` takes O(n) per step, leading to O(n^2) time. Converting to an array and using two pointers allows us to swap in-place, achieving O(n) time complexity.
